source_note: OWASP Top 10:2025 fetched from https://top10.owasp.org/2025/ ; CWE Top 25 (2025) fetched from https://cwe.mitre.org/top25/archive/2025/2025_cwe_top25.html on 2026-09-14. CWE-to-OWASP-category mapping below is this project's own best-fit judgment, not an official MITRE/OWASP crosswalk; entries with no clean web-application mapping are labeled 'General Software Weakness'. Extended: 234 further CWE entries relevant to Python/JavaScript/TypeScript code (cwe_extended). CWE ids/names follow the MITRE catalogue; descriptions, example patterns and the OWASP category mapping are project-authored.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Broken Access Control
owasp_top10_2025.description: Vulnerabilities that let unauthorized users reach resources or perform actions they should not be permitted to, e.g. viewing or modifying another user's data by changing an ID in a request.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Security Misconfiguration
owasp_top10_2025.description: Insecure default settings, incomplete hardening, verbose error messages, or unnecessary features left enabled that expose the application to attack.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
owasp_top10_2025.description: Risks introduced through compromised, outdated, or unvetted third-party dependencies, libraries, or build/deployment pipeline components.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Cryptographic Failures
owasp_top10_2025.description: Weak, missing, or misconfigured encryption, hashing, or key management that exposes sensitive data in transit or at rest.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Injection
owasp_top10_2025.description: Untrusted input is passed to an interpreter (SQL, OS shell, template engine, HTML renderer, etc.) without proper neutralisation, letting an attacker alter the intended command or query.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Insecure Design
owasp_top10_2025.description: Missing or inadequate security controls baked into the architecture itself (no threat modeling, unsafe defaults, missing rate limits) rather than a single implementation bug.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Authentication Failures
owasp_top10_2025.description: Weaknesses in verifying user identity: weak/guessable credentials, broken session management, or ways to bypass login entirely.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
owasp_top10_2025.description: Code or data that is trusted without verifying its integrity, including unsafe deserialization of untrusted data and unsigned/unverified updates.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Security Logging and Alerting Failures
owasp_top10_2025.description: Insufficient logging, monitoring, or alerting means attacks go undetected and incident response is delayed or impossible.

owasp_top10_2025.name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
owasp_top10_2025.description: Errors, exceptions, or edge cases that are not handled safely, leaking sensitive information or leaving the system in an exploitable state.

cwe_top25_2025.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-Site Scripting)
cwe_top25_2025.description: User-supplied input is written into an HTML page without proper escaping, letting an attacker run arbitrary script in another user's browser.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern:
innerHTML = userInput; document.write(userInput); render("
" + userInput + "
")

cwe_top25_2025.name: SQL Injection
cwe_top25_2025.description: User input is concatenated directly into a SQL query string instead of using parameterised queries, letting an attacker alter the query's logic.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '" + userId + "'"; query("... WHERE name='" + name + "'")

cwe_top25_2025.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cwe_top25_2025.description: A state-changing request lacks a per-session token, letting an attacker trick a logged-in user's browser into submitting it unintentionally.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: app.post('/transfer', ...) with no CSRF token check; form without anti-forgery token

cwe_top25_2025.name: Missing Authorization
cwe_top25_2025.description: An endpoint or action performs a sensitive operation without checking whether the caller is actually permitted to perform it.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: router.delete('/user/:id', (req,res)=>{ deleteUser(req.params.id) }) with no role/ownership check

cwe_top25_2025.name: Out-of-bounds Write
cwe_top25_2025.description: Data is written past the end (or before the start) of an allocated buffer, corrupting adjacent memory.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: buf[i] = value where i can exceed buf's allocated length; strcpy into a fixed buffer

cwe_top25_2025.name: Path Traversal
cwe_top25_2025.description: User-controlled input is used to build a filesystem path without sanitising '../' sequences, letting an attacker read or write files outside the intended directory.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: open(base_dir + userFilename); fs.readFile(path.join(uploadsDir, req.query.file))

cwe_top25_2025.name: Use After Free
cwe_top25_2025.description: Memory is used after it has already been freed, which can corrupt data or be exploited to hijack control flow.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: free(ptr); ...; ptr->field = x;

cwe_top25_2025.name: Out-of-bounds Read
cwe_top25_2025.description: Data is read from past the end (or before the start) of an allocated buffer, potentially leaking adjacent memory contents.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: value = buf[i] where i is not bounds-checked against buf's length

cwe_top25_2025.name: OS Command Injection
cwe_top25_2025.description: User input is concatenated into a string passed to a shell/OS command execution function, letting an attacker inject arbitrary commands.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: os.system("ping " + host); exec("convert " + filename + " out.png"); child_process.exec(`ls ${dir}`)

cwe_top25_2025.name: Code Injection
cwe_top25_2025.description: User-controlled data is passed to a function that evaluates or executes it as code (eval, template rendering, deserialisation-to-code), letting an attacker run arbitrary code.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: eval(userInput); Function(userInput)(); exec(compile(userCode))

cwe_top25_2025.name: Classic Buffer Overflow
cwe_top25_2025.description: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the source data fits, overwriting adjacent memory.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: strcpy(dest, src) with attacker-controlled src and a fixed-size dest

cwe_top25_2025.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
cwe_top25_2025.description: A file upload feature does not validate the uploaded file's type/extension, letting an attacker upload and later execute a malicious script.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: app.post('/upload', ...) saving req.file to a web-served directory with no extension/type allowlist

cwe_top25_2025.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
cwe_top25_2025.description: A pointer/reference that can be null is dereferenced without a null check, crashing the program or, in some contexts, exposing an exploitable state.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: user.getProfile().getName() where getProfile() can return null/None with no check

cwe_top25_2025.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
cwe_top25_2025.description: A buffer overflow specifically on the call stack, which can overwrite the return address and hijack control flow.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: char buf[16]; gets(buf); // or scanf("%s", buf) with unbounded input

cwe_top25_2025.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwe_top25_2025.description: Untrusted, attacker-controlled data is deserialised (e.g. pickle, Java serialization, YAML.load) without validation, which can lead to arbitrary code execution.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: pickle.loads(request.data); yaml.load(user_input); ObjectInputStream.readObject() on untrusted bytes

cwe_top25_2025.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
cwe_top25_2025.description: A buffer overflow on heap-allocated memory, which can corrupt heap metadata or adjacent objects.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: malloc(n); memcpy(heapBuf, src, largerThanN)

cwe_top25_2025.name: Incorrect Authorization
cwe_top25_2025.description: An authorization check exists but is implemented incorrectly (wrong role compared, missing edge case), letting some unauthorized requests through.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: if (user.role != 'admin') { /* allow */ } — inverted or incomplete condition

cwe_top25_2025.name: Improper Input Validation
cwe_top25_2025.description: Input is not validated (type, length, format, range) before being used, which is the root cause underlying many injection and logic-error vulnerabilities.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: age = int(request.form['age']) used directly with no range/type check before a privileged operation

cwe_top25_2025.name: Improper Access Control
cwe_top25_2025.description: The general weakness of not properly restricting access to a resource, of which missing/incorrect authorization are specific sub-cases.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: an internal admin route reachable without any auth middleware attached

cwe_top25_2025.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwe_top25_2025.description: Sensitive data (secrets, stack traces, internal paths, PII) is exposed to a party that should not have access to it, e.g. in an error message or API response.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: return { error: err.stack } in an API response; logging full request bodies containing passwords

cwe_top25_2025.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwe_top25_2025.description: A sensitive operation (e.g. changing a password, admin action) can be invoked without the caller being authenticated at all.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: router.post('/admin/reset-password', ...) with no auth middleware in front of it

cwe_top25_2025.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
cwe_top25_2025.description: The server fetches a URL supplied (directly or indirectly) by the user without restriction, letting an attacker make the server reach internal-only endpoints.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: requests.get(user_supplied_url); fetch(req.body.callbackUrl)

cwe_top25_2025.name: Command Injection
cwe_top25_2025.description: General case of untrusted input reaching a command interpreter, letting an attacker inject additional commands or arguments.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: subprocess.run(user_input, shell=True)

cwe_top25_2025.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
cwe_top25_2025.description: An object/record is looked up using a key or ID taken directly from user input, with no check that the requester actually owns that object (a.k.a. IDOR).
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: GET /api/orders/:id -> db.orders.findById(req.params.id) with no ownership check against req.user

cwe_top25_2025.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
cwe_top25_2025.description: An operation allocates resources (memory, threads, file handles, DB connections) in response to user input with no cap, enabling denial-of-service.
cwe_top25_2025.example_pattern: for each request, spawn an unbounded worker; accept an unbounded file upload size

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component (Injection)
cwe_extended.description: Untrusted data is placed into a command, query, message or document handed to another component without neutralising characters that component treats as syntax, letting the attacker change its meaning.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: build a string from request data and pass it to an interpreter, database, shell, template or protocol handler

cwe_extended.name: Argument Injection or Modification
cwe_extended.description: User input is passed as an argument to an external program without preventing it from being parsed as an extra option or flag, so the attacker changes what the program does (for example --output, -exec, --upload-pack).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: subprocess.run(['git','clone',url]) where url starts with a dash; spawn('curl', [userUrl]); options from request

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is concatenated into an LDAP search filter or distinguished name without escaping, allowing filter manipulation, authentication bypass or directory data disclosure.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ldap.search('(&(uid=' + user + ')(userPassword=' + pw + '))')

cwe_extended.name: XML Injection (Blind XPath Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is inserted into an XML document or XPath-style query without neutralising markup characters, allowing the attacker to alter the structure or content of the XML.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: xml = '<user><name>' + name + '</name></user>'; building xml elements by string concatenation

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences (CRLF Injection)
cwe_extended.description: Carriage-return and line-feed characters from user input are written into a protocol message, log or header block, letting the attacker inject extra lines or headers.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: response.setHeader('X-Name', req.query.name); header value containing \r\n

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input reaches an evaluation function that interprets strings as code, so the attacker can run arbitrary code in the application.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: eval(user_input); exec(code); new Function(body); vm.runInNewContext(userCode); setTimeout(string)

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code (Static Code Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is written into a source file, template or configuration that is later executed or included, so attacker-controlled text becomes code.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open('settings.py','a').write('LEVEL = ' + value); writing user text into a .js or .py file that is later loaded

cwe_extended.name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers (Resource Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is used as an identifier of a resource such as a file name, port, socket, queue, bucket or table, letting the attacker reach resources the application did not intend to expose.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open(request.args['name']); s3.get_object(Bucket=user_bucket); connect(host, int(port_from_user))

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers (HTTP Response Splitting)
cwe_extended.description: User input containing line breaks is copied into an HTTP response header, so the attacker can inject headers or split the response into two, enabling cache poisoning or XSS.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: res.setHeader('Location', req.query.url); response['Set-Cookie'] = 'lang=' + lang; redirect with unvalidated value

cwe_extended.name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
cwe_extended.description: Data is written to an output context (HTML, URL, JavaScript, SQL, shell, JSON) without the encoding that context requires, so special characters are interpreted as syntax.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: string concatenation into HTML attribute, URL or script block without context-specific encoding

cwe_extended.name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User-controlled text is written to a log without removing line breaks or control characters, letting an attacker forge log entries or hide activity.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: logger.info('login failed for ' + username); console.log(req.body.comment)

cwe_extended.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
cwe_extended.description: A format string passed to a formatting function comes from user input, so format directives can read internal data or cause errors (for example str.format on attacker text exposes object attributes).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: user_template.format(**ctx); '{0.__class__}'.format(obj); printf-style call with user format

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements
cwe_extended.description: Special characters or delimiters in input are not neutralised before the data is used by a component that gives them structural meaning.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: split input on a delimiter then trust the pieces; building CSV, key=value or protocol lines from raw input

cwe_extended.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code (Unsafe Reflection)
cwe_extended.description: User input chooses which class, function, module or method is loaded or called, so the attacker can run unintended code paths or instantiate dangerous classes.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: importlib.import_module(request.args['mod']); getattr(obj, user_attr)(); require(userPath); window[userFunction]()

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions (XPath Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is concatenated into an XPath expression, letting the attacker alter the query to read other nodes or bypass authentication.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: tree.xpath("//user[name='" + name + "' and pass='" + pw + "']")

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement (Expression Language Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is evaluated by an expression language engine (SpEL, OGNL, EL, JEXL, template expression engines), allowing arbitrary expression and often code execution.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: evaluate(userExpression); expression engine parse(user_text).getValue()

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User-supplied objects or strings are passed straight into a NoSQL query (MongoDB, CouchDB, Elasticsearch), so operators such as $ne, $gt or $where change the query logic.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: db.users.find({username: req.body.username, password: req.body.password}); collection.find(request.json); $where with user string

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File (CSV Injection)
cwe_extended.description: Cell values that begin with =, +, - or @ are exported to CSV/spreadsheet files without neutralisation, so opening the file in a spreadsheet runs attacker formulas.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: csv.writer.writerow([user_name, comment]); export rows containing raw user text starting with =

cwe_extended.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution)
cwe_extended.description: A merge, clone or property-assignment routine copies attacker-controlled keys such as __proto__, constructor or prototype into objects, changing behaviour of every object in the process.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: merge(target, JSON.parse(body)); obj[key][subkey] = value with keys from input; lodash.merge defaultsDeep unsafe

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (Server-Side Template Injection)
cwe_extended.description: User input is placed into the template source (not into its data), so the template engine evaluates attacker expressions and can reach code execution.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: render_template_string(user_text); Template(user_input).render(); ejs.render(req.query.t); nunjucks.renderString(input)

cwe_extended.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)
cwe_extended.description: An XML parser is run with external entity or DTD processing enabled on untrusted XML, letting the attacker read local files, make server-side requests or exhaust resources.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: etree.parse(user_xml); xml2js / libxmljs with noent true; DocumentBuilder without disabling doctype; lxml resolve_entities True

cwe_extended.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs (XML Entity Expansion)
cwe_extended.description: An XML parser expands nested entity definitions in untrusted input without limits, so a small document expands to gigabytes (billion laughs) and exhausts memory or CPU.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(untrusted); parsers without entity expansion limits

cwe_extended.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
cwe_extended.description: The application redirects the user to a URL taken from a request parameter without checking that it points to an allowed destination, which attackers use for phishing.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return redirect(request.args['next']); res.redirect(req.query.url); Location header from user input

cwe_extended.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity (ReDoS)
cwe_extended.description: A regular expression with nested or overlapping quantifiers is matched against attacker-controlled input, so backtracking takes exponential time and blocks the process.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: re.match('(a+)+$', user); new RegExp(userPattern); /^(\w+\s?)*$/.test(input)

cwe_extended.name: Permissive Regular Expression
cwe_extended.description: A regular expression used for validation is unanchored or too broad, so inputs that should be rejected still match (for example missing ^ and $, or an unescaped dot in a domain check).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: re.search('example.com', url); /admin/.test(path); allow-list pattern without anchors

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting (Prompt Injection)
cwe_extended.description: Untrusted text is concatenated into a prompt for a language model, so instructions hidden in that text can override the developer's instructions or trigger unintended tool calls and data disclosure.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: prompt = f"Summarise this document: {user_document}"; llm tools executed from model output without checks

cwe_extended.name: Improper Validation of Generative AI Output
cwe_extended.description: Output of a language model is trusted and used directly as code, a command, SQL, HTML or a security decision without validation or sandboxing.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: exec(llm_response); subprocess.run(model_output, shell=True); innerHTML = completion; cursor.execute(generated_sql)

cwe_extended.name: Relative Path Traversal
cwe_extended.description: A path built from user input contains sequences such as ../ that move outside the intended directory, exposing or overwriting other files.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open(os.path.join(BASE, filename)); fs.readFile(path.join(dir, req.query.f)); send_file(user_path)

cwe_extended.name: Absolute Path Traversal
cwe_extended.description: User input supplies a full absolute path (such as /etc/passwd or C:\\Windows\\win.ini) that the application opens without restricting it to an allowed directory.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open(request.args['file']); fs.createReadStream(req.params.path); absolute path accepted from request

cwe_extended.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access (Link Following)
cwe_extended.description: The application accesses a file path without checking whether it is a symbolic link or junction, so an attacker can point it at a sensitive target.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open(path) on files in a shared or user-writable directory; extracting archives that contain symlinks

cwe_extended.name: External Control of File Name or Path
cwe_extended.description: A file name or path used for reading, writing, deleting or including comes from user input, letting the attacker choose which file is affected.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.remove(request.form['file']); open(user_path, 'w'); fs.unlink(req.body.name); import by user path

cwe_extended.name: Insecure Temporary File
cwe_extended.description: A temporary file is created with a predictable name or in a shared directory without exclusive creation, allowing other users to pre-create, read or replace it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open('/tmp/report.txt','w'); tempfile.mktemp(); fs.writeFile('/tmp/' + name)

cwe_extended.name: Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions
cwe_extended.description: A temporary file or directory is created in a location or with permissions that let other local users read or modify it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.makedirs('/tmp/app', mode=0o777); chmod 777 tmp file; world-writable temp directory

cwe_extended.name: Direct Request (Forced Browsing)
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive pages, endpoints or files are reachable by requesting their URL directly because access control is applied only to links in the interface, not on the server.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: admin routes registered without auth decorator; static export or backup files served; hidden URLs assumed secret

cwe_extended.name: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary (Confused Deputy)
cwe_extended.description: The application forwards a request on behalf of a user to another service using its own privileges or credentials, allowing the user to reach things they could not reach directly.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: proxy endpoint forwards arbitrary URL with server credentials; internal API called with service token using user-chosen path

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
cwe_extended.description: System details such as paths, versions, environment variables, configuration or stack data are returned to users who should not see them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return jsonify(dict(os.environ)); debug endpoint printing config; phpinfo style status page

cwe_extended.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
cwe_extended.description: Secrets or personal data are written to files in a web-served, shared or public location where unauthorised people can fetch them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: write credentials to public/ or static/ folder; save backups or exports under the web root

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing
cwe_extended.description: The server shows the contents of a directory when no index file exists, revealing file names and structure.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: express.static with serve-index; autoindex on; python -m http.server style listing of data directories

cwe_extended.name: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
cwe_extended.description: Files that should be private (source, configuration, dumps, keys, version-control folders) are located where a web server or file share can deliver them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app.use(express.static('.')); serving project root; .git or .env reachable over HTTP

cwe_extended.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled SQL Primary Key
cwe_extended.description: A record is fetched or changed using an id from the request without checking that the record belongs to the current user.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ? with id from URL and no owner check; Model.objects.get(pk=request.GET['id'])

cwe_extended.name: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
cwe_extended.description: Passwords, tokens or personal data are sent in the URL query string of GET requests, where they are stored in logs, history and referrer headers.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requests.get(url, params={'password': pw}); fetch('/login?token=' + token); <form method=get> with password field

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
cwe_extended.description: A resource is made reachable to a wider audience than intended, such as binding a debug service to all interfaces or making an object store public.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True); bucket ACL public-read; internal service listening on public interface

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwe_extended.description: Files, directories, sockets or keys are created with permissions that let other users read or modify them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.chmod(path, 0o777); open key file with mode 0o666; umask(0); fs.chmodSync(file, 0o777)

cwe_extended.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
cwe_extended.description: A powerful method (file access, command execution, reload, admin) is exposed through an API, RPC, WebView bridge or message handler without restriction.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: jsonrpc dispatch of arbitrary method names; electron contextBridge exposing fs and child_process; exposed eval endpoint

cwe_extended.name: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive data is stored without access protection or encryption, for example in browser localStorage, world-readable files or plain preferences.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: localStorage.setItem('token', jwt); sessionStorage password; sensitive data in a plain file

cwe_extended.name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
cwe_extended.description: A session or authentication cookie is set with SameSite=None or without the attribute, so browsers send it on cross-site requests and CSRF becomes easier.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: res.cookie('session', id, {sameSite: 'none'}); Set-Cookie without SameSite; SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None

cwe_extended.name: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
cwe_extended.description: A session or authentication cookie is created without the HttpOnly attribute, so scripts running in the page (for example through XSS) can read it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: res.cookie('sid', id); response.set_cookie('session', value); SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False

cwe_extended.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute
cwe_extended.description: A cookie holding session or credential data is not marked Secure, so browsers may send it over plain HTTP where it can be intercepted.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: res.cookie('sid', id, {secure: false}); SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False; set_cookie without secure=True

cwe_extended.name: Origin Validation Error
cwe_extended.description: The application trusts the origin, host or referrer of a request or message without validating it properly, for example reflecting any Origin header or accepting postMessage from any sender.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: response['Access-Control-Allow-Origin'] = request.headers['Origin']; window.addEventListener('message', handler) with no event.origin check

cwe_extended.name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains (CORS Misconfiguration)
cwe_extended.description: A CORS or cross-domain policy allows untrusted origins, commonly a wildcard or reflected Origin combined with credentials, letting other sites read authenticated responses.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: cors({origin: true, credentials: true}); Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with cookies; CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True

cwe_extended.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes (Mass Assignment)
cwe_extended.description: Request data is bound directly onto a model or object, so users can set fields they should not control, such as role, isAdmin or price.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: User(**request.json); Object.assign(user, req.body); Model.create(req.body); serializer with fields = '__all__'

cwe_extended.name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames (Clickjacking)
cwe_extended.description: A page can be embedded in a frame by any other site because no frame-ancestors policy or X-Frame-Options header is sent, enabling clickjacking.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app without helmet frameguard; response missing X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors; X_FRAME_OPTIONS disabled

cwe_extended.name: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access
cwe_extended.description: Links opened with target=_blank without rel=noopener let the opened page control the original tab through window.opener (reverse tabnabbing).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: <a href=userUrl target="_blank">; window.open(url) without noopener

cwe_extended.name: Improper Privilege Management
cwe_extended.description: Privileges are assigned, retained or elevated incorrectly, so a user or process can act with more rights than intended.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: user.role = request.json['role']; setuid left active; privilege added without checking caller; admin flag from client

cwe_extended.name: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
cwe_extended.description: Code runs with higher privileges than it needs, such as as root or administrator, so any flaw in it has a larger impact.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: container user root; sudo in application code; service running with admin token for read-only work

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Default Permissions
cwe_extended.description: Files, directories or resources are installed or created with default permissions that are too open.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: default umask 000; shared config created world-readable; default ACL allows everyone

cwe_extended.name: Improper Authorization
cwe_extended.description: The application does not correctly check that the actor is allowed to perform an action on a resource, or the check can be bypassed.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: permission check only in UI; role compared incorrectly; authorisation skipped on some code path

cwe_extended.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwe_extended.description: A password, API key, token or cryptographic key is written into source code or a committed config file, so anyone with the code (or the binary) can authenticate and the secret cannot be rotated without a redeploy.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: API_KEY = 'sk_live_...'; password = 'admin123'; const secret = 'changeme'; Authorization header with literal token

cwe_extended.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
cwe_extended.description: A fixed password is compiled into the program or stored in a config checked into version control and used for authentication or to decrypt data.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: DB_PASSWORD = 'root'; if password == 'letmein': grant access

cwe_extended.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
cwe_extended.description: A symmetric key, HMAC secret or signing key is embedded in source code, so anyone who sees the code can decrypt data or forge signed tokens.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: KEY = b'0123456789abcdef'; jwt.encode(payload, 'secret', algorithm='HS256'); crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-cbc', 'fixedkey', iv)

cwe_extended.name: Plaintext Storage of a Password
cwe_extended.description: Passwords are stored or written unprotected (plain text, reversible encoding) instead of salted one-way hashes, so a database or file leak exposes every user's password.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: user.password = request.form['password']; db.insert({password: req.body.password}); base64 of a password

cwe_extended.name: Storing Passwords in a Recoverable Format
cwe_extended.description: Passwords are stored encrypted or encoded so they can be recovered, rather than hashed, so one stolen key reveals all passwords.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: encrypt(password, key); base64.b64encode(password); store reversible cipher

cwe_extended.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
cwe_extended.description: Credentials are transmitted or stored in a way that lets attackers obtain them, for example in URLs, logs, cookies without protection, or unencrypted configuration.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requests.get(url + '?password=' + pw); localStorage.setItem('password', pw); credentials in query string

cwe_extended.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
cwe_extended.description: A key length or algorithm parameter is too small for the protection required, such as RSA below 2048 bits, AES keys under 128 bits, or short HMAC keys, which makes brute force or factoring feasible.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=512); RSA.generate(1024); DES key

cwe_extended.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwe_extended.description: The code uses a cryptographic primitive known to be weak or obsolete (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, ECB mode) for security purposes such as password hashing, signatures or encryption.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: hashlib.md5(password.encode()); crypto.createHash('sha1'); AES.new(key, AES.MODE_ECB); DES.new

cwe_extended.name: Use of Weak Hash
cwe_extended.description: A hash function that is too fast or collision-prone (MD5, SHA-1, unsalted SHA-256) is used where collision or pre-image resistance, or slow password hashing, is required.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest(); crypto.createHash('md5').update(pw).digest('hex'); sha256(password) without salt or work factor

cwe_extended.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
cwe_extended.description: Passwords are hashed with a fast general-purpose hash or with too few iterations, so stolen hashes can be cracked quickly with GPUs, instead of using bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2 with a high work factor.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(); pbkdf2_hmac('sha1', pw, salt, 1000); bcrypt cost 4

cwe_extended.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
cwe_extended.description: Passwords are hashed without a unique per-user salt so identical passwords give identical hashes and precomputed rainbow tables work.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() with no salt; md5(pw)

cwe_extended.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
cwe_extended.description: The salt for password hashing is constant, derived from the username or otherwise predictable, which allows precomputation attacks across users.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: salt = 'static_salt'; salt = username; hash(pw + username)

cwe_extended.name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
cwe_extended.description: Security-relevant values such as tokens, session ids, reset codes or keys are generated with a predictable random source instead of a cryptographically secure generator.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: random.randint(100000, 999999); Math.random().toString(36); random.choice(string.ascii_letters); uuid1 token

cwe_extended.name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
cwe_extended.description: A non-cryptographic PRNG (Python random module, JavaScript Math.random, rand()) is used to produce secrets, so outputs can be predicted from a few observed values.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: token = ''.join(random.choice(chars) for _ in range(32)); const id = Math.random().toString(16); random.seed(time.time())

cwe_extended.name: Insufficient Entropy
cwe_extended.description: Random values drawn from a small space (a few digits, a timestamp, a counter) can be brute-forced or guessed, even when a strong generator is used.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: otp = random 4 digits; token = str(int(time.time())); session id = counter

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Usage of Seeds in Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
cwe_extended.description: A PRNG is seeded with a fixed or predictable value (constant, system time, process id) so the whole output sequence can be reproduced.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: random.seed(1234); random.seed(int(time.time())); srand(time(NULL))

cwe_extended.name: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
cwe_extended.description: A CBC initialization vector is constant or predictable, allowing chosen-plaintext attacks and leaking equality of messages.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: iv = b'0000000000000000'; AES.new(key, AES.MODE_CBC, iv=key[:16]); createCipheriv with fixed iv

cwe_extended.name: Reusing a Nonce, Key Pair in Encryption
cwe_extended.description: The same nonce or IV is used more than once with the same key in a stream cipher or AEAD mode such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20, which can reveal plaintext and allow forgery.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: nonce = b'000000000000'; AESGCM.encrypt(nonce, data, aad) with a fixed nonce for each message

cwe_extended.name: Missing Cryptographic Step
cwe_extended.description: A required cryptographic step is skipped, such as verifying a MAC before decrypting, using an unauthenticated cipher mode, or not signing a message, so integrity or authenticity is not protected.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: AES CBC without HMAC; decrypt then check; encrypt only with no authentication tag

cwe_extended.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
cwe_extended.description: A signature, JWT or certificate chain is not verified, or is verified in a way an attacker can bypass, for example accepting alg none, skipping verification, or decoding without checking.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}); jwt.verify with algorithms from the token header; jwt.decode(token, verify=False)

cwe_extended.name: Improper Certificate Validation
cwe_extended.description: TLS certificates are not validated, accepting any certificate and exposing the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requests.get(url, verify=False); ssl._create_unverified_context(); rejectUnauthorized: false; NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0; check_hostname = False

cwe_extended.name: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
cwe_extended.description: A certificate is accepted without checking that its hostname matches the server being contacted, so any valid certificate for another site can impersonate the server.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ssl.CERT_REQUIRED but check_hostname = False; checkServerIdentity: () => undefined

cwe_extended.name: Improper Following of a Certificate's Chain of Trust
cwe_extended.description: The code does not verify the full certificate chain up to a trusted root, accepting self-signed or untrusted certificate authorities.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: accept self-signed; custom trust manager that trusts all; ca=None; ssl context load_default_certs skipped

cwe_extended.name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive data (credentials, tokens, personal data) is sent over plain HTTP, FTP, Telnet or unencrypted sockets where network attackers can read or alter it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requests.post('http://api.example.com/login', data=creds); ftplib.FTP; smtplib without starttls; http.createServer for login

cwe_extended.name: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive data is stored or sent without any encryption although it should be protected, such as personal data in plain database fields or files.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open('users.txt','w').write(ssn); store credit card number plain; write token to a world-readable file

cwe_extended.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive information such as secrets, tokens or personal data is stored in clear text in files, databases, cookies, or browser storage.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: localStorage.setItem('token', t); config file with api key; json.dump(creds, open('creds.json','w'))

cwe_extended.name: Cleartext Storage in a File or on Disk
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive data is written to a file or disk location without encryption, readable by any local user or by anyone who obtains the disk.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open('secrets.txt','w').write(key); pickle.dump(session, f); fs.writeFileSync('token.txt', token)

cwe_extended.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in a Cookie
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive values such as passwords, tokens or personal data are placed in a cookie without encryption, exposing them to the browser, proxies and scripts.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: resp.set_cookie('password', pw); res.cookie('user', JSON.stringify(user)); document.cookie = 'ssn=' + ssn

cwe_extended.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
cwe_extended.description: Passwords, tokens, personal data or secrets are written to log files, from where operators, log aggregators and attackers with log access can read them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: logger.info('login %s %s', user, password); console.log(req.headers.authorization); log.debug(request.body)

cwe_extended.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
cwe_extended.description: Error messages shown to users include stack traces, SQL statements, file paths, or configuration details that help an attacker learn about the system.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return str(e); res.status(500).send(err.stack); traceback.format_exc() in response; app.run(debug=True)

cwe_extended.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
cwe_extended.description: Debug features, verbose error pages or diagnostic endpoints left enabled in production disclose internals and sometimes allow code execution.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app.run(debug=True); DEBUG = True; app.use(errorhandler()) in production; /debug route

cwe_extended.name: Active Debug Code
cwe_extended.description: Debug interfaces, test backdoors or developer shortcuts remain active in deployed code and can be used to bypass controls or execute commands.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app.run(debug=True) with Werkzeug debugger; if request.args.get('debug') == '1'; backdoor route

cwe_extended.name: Improper Authentication
cwe_extended.description: The code claims to authenticate an actor but does not prove the claimed identity, for example by trusting a client-supplied identity, comparing the wrong values, or skipping credential verification.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if request.headers.get('X-User'): login; user = req.query.user; password check skipped for some paths

cwe_extended.name: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
cwe_extended.description: A protected function can be reached through another route, port, method or URL that does not enforce the authentication applied to the main path.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: only /admin protected but /api/admin open; auth on GET but not POST; legacy endpoint without middleware

cwe_extended.name: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
cwe_extended.description: Identity is derived from data an attacker can forge, such as an IP address, a Host or Referer header, or a header set by a proxy.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if request.remote_addr == '127.0.0.1'; if 'X-Forwarded-For' in headers: trusted; trust Origin header for auth

cwe_extended.name: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
cwe_extended.description: Captured authentication messages or tokens can be replayed because they have no nonce, timestamp or one-time property.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: signed request without timestamp or nonce; token valid forever; HMAC over body only

cwe_extended.name: Channel Accessible by Non-Endpoint (Adversary-in-the-Middle)
cwe_extended.description: Communication lacks verification that both endpoints are authentic, enabling an intermediary to read or alter traffic.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: no certificate pinning; unauthenticated key exchange; trust any peer

cwe_extended.name: Authentication Bypass by Assumed-Immutable Data
cwe_extended.description: Authentication or authorization decisions rely on data the client controls (hidden form fields, cookies, JWT claims read without verification) that is wrongly assumed to be unchangeable.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: isAdmin from cookie; role from hidden input; trusted JWT payload decode without verify

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Implementation of Authentication Algorithm
cwe_extended.description: A standard authentication protocol or algorithm is implemented incorrectly, for example flawed challenge-response or token validation logic.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: custom HMAC comparison; home-made token scheme; skipped step in OAuth flow

cwe_extended.name: Missing Critical Step in Authentication
cwe_extended.description: A necessary check is omitted from the authentication flow, such as the second factor, an email verification or a password check.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: login succeeds on username alone; MFA step skipped when a parameter is present; verified flag ignored

cwe_extended.name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
cwe_extended.description: Login, password-reset or OTP endpoints allow unlimited guesses with no lockout, delay or rate limit, enabling brute force and credential stuffing.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: @app.route('/login', methods=['POST']) with no rate limit; otp verify endpoint without attempt counter

cwe_extended.name: Use of Single-factor Authentication
cwe_extended.description: A sensitive operation or privileged account relies only on a password with no second factor, so credential theft is enough to take over the account.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: admin login password only; privileged action without step-up

cwe_extended.name: Use of Password System for Primary Authentication
cwe_extended.description: The application depends only on passwords as the primary authentication where stronger mechanisms should be used.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: password-only authentication for high-value accounts

cwe_extended.name: Weak Password Requirements
cwe_extended.description: The application accepts weak, short or common passwords because it enforces no length, complexity or breached-password checks.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if len(password) >= 1; no validation on registration or password change; password '123456' allowed

cwe_extended.name: Unverified Password Change
cwe_extended.description: A password can be changed without confirming the current password or other proof, so a hijacked session leads to permanent takeover.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: update password with only new_password parameter; no old password check

cwe_extended.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
cwe_extended.description: The password recovery flow can be abused through guessable security questions, predictable reset tokens, tokens that do not expire, or reset links returned to the requester.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: reset_token = str(user.id) + str(int(time.time())); return the token in the API response; security question

cwe_extended.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
cwe_extended.description: Sessions, tokens or reset links remain valid for too long or after logout and password change, giving attackers who steal them a long window of use.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: jwt.encode without exp; session lifetime 10 years; logout does not invalidate server session; PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME huge

cwe_extended.name: Session Fixation
cwe_extended.description: The session identifier is not regenerated after login, so an attacker who planted a known session id before authentication shares the victim's authenticated session.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: session['user'] = user without session.clear or regenerate; accepting session id from the URL

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session
cwe_extended.description: Data from one user's session is stored in shared (global, class-level or static) state and returned to another user's request.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: module-level variable holding current user; cache keyed without user id; global request data in a singleton

cwe_extended.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
cwe_extended.description: The application trusts cookie values (roles, prices, user ids) without signing or verifying them, so users can edit them freely.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: role = request.cookies.get('role'); if req.cookies.isAdmin == 'true'; price from cookie

cwe_extended.name: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter
cwe_extended.description: Parameters the application believes the user cannot change (hidden fields, prices, ids, flags) are accepted from the request and used to make security or business decisions.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: total = request.form['price']; hidden input is_admin; trusting amount from client

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
cwe_extended.description: New users or roles are granted more privileges than intended, for example admin as default role or inherited broad permissions.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: user.role = 'admin' on signup; default permissions all; is_staff=True

cwe_extended.name: Privilege Defined With Unsafe Actions
cwe_extended.description: A privilege or role is defined so broadly that holders can perform dangerous actions beyond their purpose.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: role 'support' can delete users; token scope '*'

cwe_extended.name: Privilege Chaining
cwe_extended.description: Two privileges that are safe separately combine to allow privilege escalation, for example the ability to write a script and the ability to schedule it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: user can edit template and trigger render as admin

cwe_extended.name: Privilege Context Switching Error
cwe_extended.description: Privileges are not properly dropped or restored when switching context, so code continues running with elevated rights.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: setuid(0) then user code; sudo for whole script; seteuid not restored

cwe_extended.name: Privilege Dropping / Lowering Errors
cwe_extended.description: A process fails to reduce its privileges after startup, or the drop does not actually take effect.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.setuid(1000) unchecked; run as root in container; USER root in Dockerfile

cwe_extended.name: Least Privilege Violation
cwe_extended.description: Code keeps elevated privileges longer than needed, giving more power to anything that goes wrong while elevated.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: run whole server as root; DB account with all privileges; admin API key for read-only task

cwe_extended.name: Improper Handling of Insufficient Privileges
cwe_extended.description: When an operation lacks the required privilege, the code ignores the failure or continues in an unsafe state instead of stopping.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: try: do_privileged() except PermissionError: pass; continue with partial rights

cwe_extended.name: Improper Handling of Insufficient Permissions or Privileges
cwe_extended.description: Permission failures are not handled, leaving the program in an insecure fallback mode such as running with default allow.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: except PermissionError: allow; default allow on lookup failure; fail open

cwe_extended.name: Use of Less Trusted Source
cwe_extended.description: The code takes security-relevant data from a source an attacker can influence, such as the first or last X-Forwarded-For entry or a client-controlled header, when a more trusted one exists.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ip = request.headers['X-Forwarded-For']; ip = req.headers['x-real-ip']; trust proxy true

cwe_extended.name: Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution for a Security-Critical Action
cwe_extended.description: Access decisions rely on reverse DNS lookups, which an attacker who controls the PTR record can forge.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: socket.gethostbyaddr(ip) to allow host; if hostname.endswith('.corp.com')

cwe_extended.name: Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard
cwe_extended.description: A security check required by a standard or protocol is implemented incorrectly or only partly, leaving gaps.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: partial signature check; JWT audience or issuer not verified; OAuth state parameter ignored

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwe_extended.description: Personal data such as emails, phone numbers, addresses or health information is returned or shared with parties that are not authorised to see it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return user.to_dict() including email and phone; GET /users returns all profile fields

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
cwe_extended.description: Data intended to be private under one policy is exposed through another feature, such as an export, API or search endpoint, with a different policy.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: export endpoint ignores field-level privacy; search reveals private records

cwe_extended.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
cwe_extended.description: Responses or messages include sensitive fields that the recipient should not receive, such as password hashes or internal ids.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return jsonify(user.__dict__); res.json(user) including password hash; serializer fields = '__all__'

cwe_extended.name: Observable Response Discrepancy
cwe_extended.description: Different responses for existing and non-existing accounts (messages, status codes, timing) let attackers enumerate valid usernames or emails.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return 'user not found' vs 'wrong password'; password reset says email not registered

cwe_extended.name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
cwe_extended.description: A comparison of secrets that exits early on the first mismatch leaks timing differences, letting attackers recover tokens or MACs byte by byte.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if token == expected; signature == computed; hmac digest compared with ==

cwe_extended.name: Observable Discrepancy
cwe_extended.description: Observable differences in behaviour, such as error text, response size or timing, reveal internal state that an attacker can use.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: distinct error for each failure step; long response only when record exists

cwe_extended.name: Unprotected Transport of Credentials
cwe_extended.description: Login forms or credential-bearing requests are served or submitted over unencrypted HTTP, exposing credentials on the network.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: <form action='http://...' method=post>; fetch('http://api/login'); Basic auth over http

cwe_extended.name: Missing Password Field Masking
cwe_extended.description: Password inputs are displayed in clear text on screen or echoed in the terminal, enabling shoulder surfing.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: <input type='text' name='password'>; input('Password: ') instead of getpass

cwe_extended.name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
cwe_extended.description: The server accepts the stored password hash as the credential itself, so anyone who steals the hash can log in without cracking it (pass-the-hash).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: compare client-sent hash with stored hash; login with hash param

cwe_extended.name: Weak Authentication
cwe_extended.description: The authentication mechanism is weak enough to be bypassed or guessed, such as simple tokens, shared secrets or trusting easily guessed identifiers.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: static API token compared with ==; Basic auth with default credentials; token = user_id

cwe_extended.name: Use of Weak Credentials
cwe_extended.description: Default, empty, common or otherwise easily guessed credentials are used for accounts or services.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: admin/admin; password=''; default postgres credentials; changeme

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
cwe_extended.description: User-controlled data containing script tags or event handlers is written into HTML without neutralising angle brackets and quotes.
cwe_extended.example_pattern:
res.send('

' + req.query.name + '

'); return '

' + name + '

'; f-string HTML response

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page
cwe_extended.description: User data is inserted into an HTML attribute value or event handler (onclick, href, src, style) without attribute encoding, allowing script injection through quotes or javascript: URLs.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ``; ; element.setAttribute('onclick', userInput); href = user url

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Encoded URI Schemes in a Web Page
cwe_extended.description: URL filters that block javascript: or data: schemes can be bypassed with encoded or whitespace-obfuscated variants that browsers still execute.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if 'javascript:' in url; startswith('http') after decoding; blacklist of schemes

cwe_extended.name: Doubled Character XSS Manipulations
cwe_extended.description: Sanitisers that remove dangerous strings once can be defeated by doubled or nested payloads, for example <scr<script>ipt>.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: replace('<script>', ''); re.sub('<script>', '', s) single pass; strip tags with a regex

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Alternate XSS Syntax
cwe_extended.description: Filters that only block obvious script tags miss alternate syntaxes such as SVG, MathML, event attributes or style expressions.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: blacklist of <script>; allow <svg>; bad regex sanitiser

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in an Error Message Web Page
cwe_extended.description: Error pages that echo user input (the bad value, the URL, the parameter name) without escaping allow reflected script injection.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return f'Invalid value: {value}'; 404 page with the requested path; res.status(400).send('Bad ' + req.query.x)

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes of IMG Tags in a Web Page
cwe_extended.description: User data is used for an image src or alt attribute without validation, enabling script or tracking injection.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ``; img.src = location.hash

cwe_extended.name: Improper Neutralization of Invalid Characters in Identifiers in Web Pages
cwe_extended.description: Invalid or unusual characters in tag names or attribute names are not handled and can be used to smuggle script.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: createElement(userTag); setAttribute(userName, value); dynamic attribute names

cwe_extended.name: SQL Injection: Hibernate
cwe_extended.description: ORM raw-query or HQL/JPQL string building with untrusted data bypasses the ORM's parameter binding and leads to SQL injection.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: session.createQuery('from User where name=' + name); Model.objects.raw(f'SELECT ... {x}'); sequelize.query(`... ${x}`); knex.raw(userInput); text(f'...')

cwe_extended.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
cwe_extended.description: Arithmetic on integers produces a value outside the representable range, wrapping around and producing a small or negative result that is used for a size, index or price. Relevant in JavaScript for numbers above 2^53 and in typed arrays.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: total = a * b with no bounds check; Number(userId) above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; Buffer.alloc(a * b); int32 wrap

cwe_extended.name: Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound)
cwe_extended.description: Subtracting a larger value from a smaller unsigned or bounded value yields a huge number that is then used as a length or index.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: remaining = len - offset with no check; quantity - requested becomes negative and passes validation

cwe_extended.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
cwe_extended.description: An array or list index derived from user input is used without checking that it lies within bounds, causing exceptions, out-of-range reads or logic bypass.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: items[int(request.args['i'])]; arr[req.query.index]; list[idx] without range check

cwe_extended.name: Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency
cwe_extended.description: A length field supplied with data is trusted instead of the real data size, causing over-reads, truncation or buffer errors.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: data[:header.length]; buf.slice(0, msg.len); trust content-length

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
cwe_extended.description: The size of a buffer, allocation or loop bound is computed incorrectly, often off by one or ignoring encoding overhead, leading to overflow or truncation.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: Buffer.alloc(str.length) for multibyte data; allocate len without terminator; off by one

cwe_extended.name: Off-by-one Error
cwe_extended.description: A loop bound or comparison is wrong by one (<= instead of <, length instead of length-1), reading or writing one item beyond the end.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: for i in range(len(a)+1); for (i = 0; i <= arr.length; i++); a[len(a)]

cwe_extended.name: Numeric Truncation Error
cwe_extended.description: A numeric value is converted to a smaller type or lower precision and silently loses information, such as float to int or 64-bit to 32-bit.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: int(float_value); value bitwise-or zero in JavaScript; Number to Int32; parseInt on large id

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
cwe_extended.description: Conversion between numeric types changes the value in a way that affects a security decision, such as signed to unsigned or string to number with trailing characters.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: parseInt('12abc'); int(user) in a limit check; Number(value) permits hex or exponent

cwe_extended.name: Insufficient Precision or Accuracy of a Real Number
cwe_extended.description: Floating-point arithmetic is used where exact results are needed, such as money, giving rounding errors that can be exploited.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: price * 1.1 as float; total += 0.1; balance float calculations

cwe_extended.name: Divide By Zero
cwe_extended.description: A divisor derived from input can be zero and the case is not handled, raising an unhandled exception or producing Infinity/NaN that corrupts later logic.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: avg = total / count; rate = a / int(request.args['b']); x % user_value

cwe_extended.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
cwe_extended.description: Return values, empty results, timeouts, or error codes are not checked, so the program continues with invalid data or an unexpected state.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ignored return value; first = rows[0] without empty check; response.json() without checking status

cwe_extended.name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
cwe_extended.description: Exceptions or failures are handled incorrectly, such as catching everything and continuing, or exposing the exception, leaving the system in an inconsistent or insecure state.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: except Exception: pass; catch (e) {} ; try/except around security check that allows on failure

cwe_extended.name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
cwe_extended.description: The software does not anticipate or properly handle unusual conditions during normal operation.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: no try/except around parsing of untrusted data; unhandled promise rejection

cwe_extended.name: Uncaught Exception
cwe_extended.description: An exception is not caught and terminates the thread or process, allowing an attacker who can trigger it to cause denial of service.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: JSON.parse(req.body) without try/catch in a handler; process.on('uncaughtException') missing; async handler without catch

cwe_extended.name: Unchecked Return Value
cwe_extended.description: The return value of a function that signals failure is ignored, so the program proceeds as if the operation succeeded.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: subprocess.run(cmd) with no check; os.chmod result ignored; fs.write callback err ignored; verify() result not used

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Check of Function Return Value
cwe_extended.description: The return value is checked with the wrong condition, treating a failure code as success or the opposite.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if not verify_signature(): continue as valid; if (strcmp(...)) allow; inverted check

cwe_extended.name: Unchecked Error Condition
cwe_extended.description: Error conditions are neither detected nor handled, for example empty exception handlers that hide failed security-relevant operations.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: try: verify() except: pass; catch(e){} around authentication

cwe_extended.name: Missing Report of Error Condition
cwe_extended.description: The program fails silently, giving neither the caller nor an operator any signal that an operation failed.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return None on error without logging; fire-and-forget promise without catch

cwe_extended.name: Return of Wrong Status Code
cwe_extended.description: A function returns a status that does not match its outcome, such as success on failure or a generic code, causing callers to make wrong decisions.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return True in finally; always return 200; return 0 on error

cwe_extended.name: Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
cwe_extended.description: Catching the broadest exception type hides specific failures and may mask security-relevant errors.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: except Exception as e: log; catch (Exception e); except:

cwe_extended.name: Declaration of Throws for Generic Exception
cwe_extended.description: A function declares or raises only a generic exception type, forcing callers to catch too broadly.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: raise Exception('failed'); throw new Error(); declared throws Exception

cwe_extended.name: Improper Cleanup on Thrown Exception
cwe_extended.description: When an exception occurs, locks, files, transactions or temporary state are not released or rolled back, leaving the system inconsistent or deadlocked.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: lock.acquire() without finally; open() without with; transaction not rolled back on error

cwe_extended.name: Missing Standardized Error Handling Mechanism
cwe_extended.description: There is no consistent error handling strategy, so different paths leak different details or skip handling.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: handlers each catch differently; no global error middleware

cwe_extended.name: Not Failing Securely (Failing Open)
cwe_extended.description: When an error or exception occurs the system defaults to a permissive state, for example granting access if the authorization service throws.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: try: allowed = check(user) except: allowed = True; default allow on timeout

cwe_extended.name: Missing Custom Error Page
cwe_extended.description: Default framework error pages are shown to users, leaking technology and internals.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: no custom 404 or 500 handler; default server error page

cwe_extended.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization (Race Condition)
cwe_extended.description: Multiple threads, processes or requests access a shared resource without proper locking, so timing decides the outcome and checks can be invalidated before use.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: balance = get(); if balance >= amt: set(balance - amt); check coupon used then mark used; non-atomic read-modify-write

cwe_extended.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
cwe_extended.description: A resource is checked and then used later, and the state can change in between, letting an attacker swap a file, link or record after the check.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if os.path.exists(p): open(p); if os.access(p): open(p); check balance then deduct in separate statements

cwe_extended.name: Signal Handler Race Condition
cwe_extended.description: A signal handler shares state with normal code without safe synchronisation and can corrupt it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: signal.signal(SIGINT, handler) modifying global structures

cwe_extended.name: Race Condition within a Thread
cwe_extended.description: Shared data within a process is accessed by multiple threads without synchronisation, leading to corrupted or inconsistent state.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: global counter incremented in threads; dict mutated by multiple threads without lock

cwe_extended.name: Context Switching Race Condition
cwe_extended.description: A sequence of privileged operations can be interrupted by a context switch that lets an attacker act between steps.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: multi-step privileged flow without atomicity

cwe_extended.name: Improper Resource Locking
cwe_extended.description: A resource is not locked, or locked inconsistently, so concurrent users can modify it simultaneously.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: no SELECT FOR UPDATE; file written without flock; optimistic update missing version check

cwe_extended.name: Missing Lock Check
cwe_extended.description: The code uses a resource without checking that the lock protecting it is held.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: use shared state without acquiring lock

cwe_extended.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
cwe_extended.description: Shared mutable data in a multithreaded server (module globals, class attributes, singletons) is modified per request without synchronisation.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: module-level dict updated per request; class attribute mutated in view; singleton with state

cwe_extended.name: Improper Synchronization
cwe_extended.description: Synchronization primitives are missing or misused, producing races, lost updates, or deadlocks.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: lock acquired in different orders; no lock around update; await missing

cwe_extended.name: Improper Locking
cwe_extended.description: Locking is applied wrongly, for example never released, taken twice, or protecting the wrong data.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: lock.acquire() without release; lock released twice

cwe_extended.name: Deadlock
cwe_extended.description: Two or more tasks wait for each other forever, so the service stops responding.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: acquire A then B in one thread and B then A in another; nested locks

cwe_extended.name: Missing Synchronization
cwe_extended.description: A resource shared between threads is used without any synchronisation at all.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: shared list append across threads; global cache dict update without lock

cwe_extended.name: Incorrect Synchronization
cwe_extended.description: A synchronization mechanism is present but incorrect, such as locking different objects or checking outside the lock.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: double-checked locking; lock created per call; check outside lock

cwe_extended.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
cwe_extended.description: Resources such as CPU, memory, disk, sockets or processes are consumed without limits, allowing an attacker to exhaust them and deny service.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: while True with request-controlled loop count; read entire upload into memory; unbounded cache; no timeout on requests

cwe_extended.name: Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)
cwe_extended.description: A small request triggers disproportionately large work or output, such as expanding compressed data, recursive queries or XML entity expansion.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: zlib.decompress(data) without a max size; unbounded zip extraction; GraphQL deeply nested queries

cwe_extended.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
cwe_extended.description: Compressed input is expanded without checking the resulting size, so a small file expands to gigabytes (zip bomb).
cwe_extended.example_pattern: zipfile.extractall(user_zip); gzip.decompress(body); tarfile.extractall without size limit

cwe_extended.name: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
cwe_extended.description: An algorithm with poor worst-case complexity (quadratic, exponential) processes attacker-controlled input, so crafted inputs cause heavy CPU usage.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: nested loops over request data; sort with custom comparator on user data; regex with catastrophic backtracking

cwe_extended.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
cwe_extended.description: Recursive processing of nested input is not depth-limited, exhausting the stack or memory and crashing the service.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: def parse(node): parse(child) on user JSON/XML; deep JSON.parse; recursion without depth

cwe_extended.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition (Infinite Loop)
cwe_extended.description: A loop can run forever for some input, blocking a worker thread or process.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: while True: read until delimiter that may never come; loop until condition user controls

cwe_extended.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
cwe_extended.description: A loop count or bound comes straight from untrusted input, letting an attacker choose very large iteration counts.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: for _ in range(int(request.args['n'])); for (let i = 0; i < req.query.count; i++)

cwe_extended.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
cwe_extended.description: A memory allocation size is taken from untrusted input without an upper bound, causing out-of-memory.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: bytearray(int(request.args['size'])); Buffer.alloc(req.body.length); [0]*n

cwe_extended.name: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling
cwe_extended.description: File handles, sockets or connections are opened without bounds or are never released, exhausting descriptors.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: open file per request without close; connection pool unlimited; socket per client without limit

cwe_extended.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
cwe_extended.description: A resource such as a file, connection or lock is never closed, leaking resources until the service fails.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: f = open(path) without close or with; connection not closed; setInterval never cleared

cwe_extended.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
cwe_extended.description: Memory held by an object remains referenced or is never freed, growing without bound over time, for example in caches, listeners and global lists.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: global list appended per request; event listener added repeatedly; cache dict without eviction

cwe_extended.name: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
cwe_extended.description: Resources are not properly closed or released on all paths, particularly error paths.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: return before close; exception skips close; no context manager

cwe_extended.name: Insufficient Resource Pool
cwe_extended.description: A pool of connections or workers is too small or unmanaged, so a small number of requests can exhaust it.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: single worker handling long requests; pool size 1; no queue

cwe_extended.name: Improper Control of Interaction Frequency
cwe_extended.description: A function that can be abused by repeated calls (sending email or SMS, creating accounts, password reset, expensive search) has no rate limiting, throttling or CAPTCHA.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: send_sms(phone) per request without limit; @app.route('/signup') unlimited; password reset email endpoint

cwe_extended.name: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action
cwe_extended.description: An action that should happen once (voting, redeeming a coupon, claiming a bonus) can be repeated because uniqueness is not enforced atomically.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: coupon redeem without used flag check; one vote per user not enforced; like endpoint adds on every call

cwe_extended.name: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
cwe_extended.description: Steps that must happen in order (payment before shipment, verification before activation) can be skipped by calling later steps directly.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ship_order(order_id) without checking paid; /confirm callable before /pay; state machine not enforced

cwe_extended.name: Business Logic Errors
cwe_extended.description: Flaws in the intended business rules allow abuse, such as negative quantities, price manipulation, or discount stacking.
