cwe_extended.example_pattern: quantity from request not validated positive; price field in request; discount applied multiple times

cwe_extended.name: Improper Use of Validation Framework
cwe_extended.description: A validation framework is available but misused or bypassed, so some inputs reach sensitive code unvalidated.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: schema defined but skipped for some routes; validate() result ignored; validation only client side

cwe_extended.name: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
cwe_extended.description: Security checks (validation, authorization, limits) are performed only in the browser or client code, which the attacker controls and can bypass.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: JavaScript form validation without server check; hiding admin buttons as only access control; client computes price

cwe_extended.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
cwe_extended.description: A security-relevant decision, such as who the user is or what they may do, depends on input an attacker can control.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: if request.args.get('admin'): grant; if req.headers['x-role'] == 'admin'; if 'internal' in referer

cwe_extended.name: External Control of Critical State Data
cwe_extended.description: Critical state such as user id, role, price or workflow stage is stored in a place the user can modify (cookie, hidden field, URL) without integrity protection.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: state kept in hidden fields; role in unsigned cookie; step number in URL

cwe_extended.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwe_extended.description: The application loads and runs code, scripts or libraries from a location or party it does not control, such as remote script URLs, user-writable directories or plugins fetched at runtime.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: importlib.import_module(user_name); require(userPath); <script src='http://cdn...'> without integrity; exec(urlopen(url).read())

cwe_extended.name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
cwe_extended.description: Third-party web content, scripts or iframes are embedded without integrity checks, so a compromise of that third party affects the page.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: <script src='https://thirdparty/x.js'> no integrity; iframe from untrusted origin

cwe_extended.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwe_extended.description: Code, updates or plugins are downloaded and executed without verifying a hash or signature, so a tampered download runs with full trust.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: urlretrieve(url, 'x.sh'); os.system('curl url then sh'); exec(requests.get(url).text); auto-update without signature

cwe_extended.name: Missing Support for Integrity Check
cwe_extended.description: Data is transmitted or stored without an integrity check such as a MAC, hash or signature, so tampering goes undetected.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: serialize state to cookie without HMAC; unsigned configuration file; message without checksum

cwe_extended.name: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value
cwe_extended.description: An integrity value is present but not verified, or is verified incorrectly, so tampered data is accepted.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: hash computed but never compared; compare with truncated digest; checksum ignored on mismatch

cwe_extended.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwe_extended.description: Data or its source is accepted without proving it is authentic, enabling forged or modified inputs, webhooks and callbacks.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: webhook handler without signature check; trust JSON from client; unsigned callback

cwe_extended.name: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data
cwe_extended.description: Untrusted data is processed together with trusted data so the untrusted part is treated with the same trust, for example unsigned fields next to signed ones.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: signed JWT with extra unsigned claims used; merging user dict into config

cwe_extended.name: Untrusted Search Path
cwe_extended.description: The program searches for executables or libraries in a directory that an attacker can control, such as the current directory or a user-writable PATH entry.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: subprocess.run('tool') relying on PATH; sys.path.insert(0, cwd); os.system('git') with writable PATH; require relative module

cwe_extended.name: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
cwe_extended.description: The search path for programs or modules includes an element controlled by users, so a malicious file can be loaded instead of the intended one.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: env PATH includes . or tmp; PYTHONPATH from user; LD_LIBRARY_PATH set from input

cwe_extended.name: Unquoted Search Path or Element
cwe_extended.description: A path containing spaces is not quoted, so the system may execute an attacker-planted program at a shorter path prefix.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: subprocess with shell and unquoted path 'C:\\Program Files\\app'; service path unquoted

cwe_extended.name: Process Control
cwe_extended.description: The application loads libraries or runs commands whose identity is controlled by an attacker, giving control over which code executes.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ctypes.CDLL(user_lib); child_process.fork(userFile); LoadLibrary from input

cwe_extended.name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
cwe_extended.description: The project depends on libraries that are abandoned or end-of-life, so known vulnerabilities will not be fixed.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requirements pinned to ancient versions; dependency last released years ago; deprecated package

cwe_extended.name: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
cwe_extended.description: The application uses a third-party package version with known vulnerabilities (CVEs), inheriting their flaws.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: requests==2.5.0; lodash 4.17.4; django 1.11 in requirements; log4j 2.14

cwe_extended.name: Using Components with Known Vulnerabilities
cwe_extended.description: Libraries, frameworks and tools with publicly known vulnerabilities are included in the build and shipped.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: old pinned library versions; no dependency scanning; vulnerable transitive dependency

cwe_extended.name: Reliance on Insufficiently Trustworthy Component
cwe_extended.description: The software relies on a component whose provenance, maintenance or security cannot be trusted, such as unknown or typo-squatted packages.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: pip install from random git URL; npm package with install scripts from unknown author; typosquatted name

cwe_extended.name: Reliance on Component That is Not Updateable
cwe_extended.description: A component is embedded or vendored in a way that prevents it from being updated when vulnerabilities are found.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: vendored copy of library edited in place; bundled minified old library; firmware fixed

cwe_extended.name: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default
cwe_extended.description: A setting, option or resource is initialised with an insecure default (open permissions, debug on, verification off) that users must remember to change.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: DEBUG=True default; CORS origins '*' by default; verify=False default; admin password default

cwe_extended.name: Configuration
cwe_extended.description: Security-relevant settings are missing, wrong or inconsistent, leaving the application or its server in an insecure configuration.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: settings.py with ALLOWED_HOSTS=['*']; SECRET_KEY in repo; helmet not used; directory listing on

cwe_extended.name: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
cwe_extended.description: An attacker can change a system or application setting through input, such as environment variables, config keys or runtime options.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.environ[user_key] = value; config[request.args['key']] = v; process.env[req.body.name]

cwe_extended.name: Password in Configuration File
cwe_extended.description: Passwords are stored in plain text in configuration files that are committed or readable by many users.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: config.ini password=secret; .env committed; application.properties password

cwe_extended.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in an Environment Variable
cwe_extended.description: Secrets placed in environment variables can leak through process listings, crash dumps, child processes and debug endpoints.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: os.environ['PASSWORD'] set for child; env passed to subprocess; printing env

cwe_extended.name: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants
cwe_extended.description: Security-sensitive values such as timeouts, limits, roles or algorithm names are hard-coded and cannot be adjusted when requirements change.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: ADMIN_ROLE_ID = 1; TOKEN_EXPIRY = 10**9; magic numbers in checks

cwe_extended.name: Use of Default Password
cwe_extended.description: Accounts or services ship or run with a known vendor or default password that is not forced to change.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: admin:admin; default superuser created with fixed password; redis without password

cwe_extended.name: Insecure Default Variable Initialization
cwe_extended.description: Variables that control security are initialised to permissive values until set otherwise.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: is_authenticated = True by default; allow = True initial; role = 'admin' default

cwe_extended.name: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address
cwe_extended.description: A service listens on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) although it should only be reachable locally or from a trusted network.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: app.run(host='0.0.0.0'); server.listen(3000, '0.0.0.0'); bind(('', port))

cwe_extended.name: Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets
cwe_extended.description: A WebSocket server accepts connections from any origin, enabling cross-site WebSocket hijacking with the victim's cookies.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: new WebSocket.Server({port}) with no verifyClient or origin check; socketio cors_allowed_origins='*'

cwe_extended.name: Use of Default Credentials
cwe_extended.description: Default credentials supplied by a product or framework remain in use.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: username: admin password: admin; guest account; sa with blank password

cwe_extended.name: Use of Default Cryptographic Key
cwe_extended.description: A default or example cryptographic key supplied with software or documentation is used in production.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: SECRET_KEY = 'your-secret-key'; example key from tutorial; demo private key committed

cwe_extended.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Metadata
cwe_extended.description: Metadata attached to files or responses (EXIF, document properties, server banners, directory listings) reveals sensitive details.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: serve uploaded images with EXIF; X-Powered-By header; autoindex on

cwe_extended.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
cwe_extended.description: A security protection mechanism is missing, disabled or ineffective, such as disabled CSRF middleware or turned-off input escaping.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: csrf_exempt on a state-changing view; autoescape=False; app.config['WTF_CSRF_ENABLED'] = False; helmet disabled

cwe_extended.name: Violation of Secure Design Principles
cwe_extended.description: The design violates basic secure design principles such as least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults or separation of duties.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: single admin token for all; no defence in depth; complete mediation missing

cwe_extended.name: Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive functions and data share the same trust domain as untrusted code, so a flaw in one part exposes everything.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: plugins running in main process; multi-tenant data in one namespace; untrusted code in same interpreter

cwe_extended.name: Trust Boundary Violation
cwe_extended.description: Untrusted data is placed into the same structure, session or variable as trusted data, making the application treat it as validated.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: session['user'] = request.args['user']; req.session.isAdmin = req.body.isAdmin; cache.set from user

cwe_extended.name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
cwe_extended.description: Messages arriving over a channel such as postMessage, a socket or an IPC endpoint are accepted without checking who sent them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: window.addEventListener('message', e => run(e.data)) without origin check; postMessage('*'); socket accepted from any peer

cwe_extended.name: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer
cwe_extended.description: Sensitive fields are not stripped from objects, files or responses before they are saved, logged or sent to another party.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: export without redaction; share logs with secrets; serializing entire user object

cwe_extended.name: Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information
cwe_extended.description: Secrets are passed on a command line or in environment visible to other processes (ps), exposing them.
cwe_extended.example_pattern: subprocess.run(['mysql', '-p' + password]); exec('curl -u user:pass'); --password=secret argument
